title: From ChatGPT discovery to merchant checkout: actors and protocol boundaries
caption: ACP carries the product feed from the merchant to ChatGPT. The ChatGPT app runs on the OpenAI Apps SDK, which is not ACP. Path A, solid lines, is the generally available external checkout on the merchant's own site. Path B, dashed lines, is the payment sheet, a private beta for select marketplace partners; only PCI DSS Level 1 merchants that want raw card data implement ACP Delegate Payment, whose request carries an allowance. No source says the payment sheet token is allowance-scoped in general.
alt: Flowchart. The merchant's catalog pushes a product feed to ChatGPT through the ACP Feed API. The shopper asks ChatGPT and picks a product, and ChatGPT opens the merchant's ChatGPT app, an MCP server and widget, through the Apps SDK. In path A the app sends the shopper an external checkout link; the shopper pays on the merchant's website, which authorizes through the merchant's PSP. In path B, drawn dashed and marked private beta, the app calls requestCheckout in ChatGPT; for PCI DSS Level 1 merchants only, ChatGPT calls the merchant's Delegate Payment vault with an allowance; ChatGPT then sends a complete_checkout tool call with a payment-method token to the app, and the app charges the token through the PSP.

sourceOfTruth.label: OpenAI Apps SDK monetization guide (read 2026-10-11), with ACP 2026-04-17
